convertibility_reason: EA uses hedging/locking logic (opening opposite positions instead of closing), which requires multi-position management and implicit position netting that is more complex than simple directional strategies. Uses only built-in indicators but the core locking mechanism is non-standard.

other_exits: Lock mechanism: instead of closing losing position, opens opposite hedge position when loss threshold reached; positions are closed as pairs when net profit target is met

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Initial trade uses fixed lots; lock (hedge) position uses same lot size as the initial position to create a neutral lock

custom_logic_notes: Core lock/hedge logic: When an open position reaches a floating loss exceeding LockStart (input parameter in pips), the EA opens an equal-sized opposite position to 'lock' the account exposure. The locked pair is then monitored; when the net floating profit of both positions combined exceeds LockProfit (input parameter), both positions are closed simultaneously. This creates a hedging cycle: entry → lock on drawdown → close pair on net profit. The EA tracks which positions are 'locked' together via magic number or comment tagging. Entry signals (EMA crossover + RSI filter) are only used for the initial directional trade, not for unlock decisions.
python_conversion_notes: Lock/hedge mechanism requires maintaining a position registry that tracks paired (locked) positions. Python implementation needs: (1) A PositionManager class that pairs long+short positions and monitors their combined P&L, (2) Careful handling of partial closes when lock profit target is hit — both sides must close atomically, (3) The lock threshold logic monitors unrealized P&L per position, not per pair, (4) Unlike standard EAs, this one can hold simultaneous long and short positions on the same symbol — ensure the broker/execution layer supports hedging mode, (5) The RSI filter values (30/70) and EMA periods (5/21) are typical defaults but should be parameterized from inputs.
